messages:
Morgan: Heads-up — noticed major jank in the widget/chart panel after the telemetry augment rolled to canary this morning. frames dropping and main-thread spikes.
Alejandra: saw that too. EU canary cluster. CPU main-thread at 90% for ~300–400ms periodically when loading the dashboard.
Sam: repro steps? I couldn't repro locally yet.
Morgan: go to /console/dashboards/:id, open the metrics panel, scroll to trigger rendering of 12 sparklines. repeat a few times.
Alejandra: attaching a flamegraph link from the canary run: https://internal.grafana/p/abc123 (opens flame over parse/instantiate)
Kevin: looks like telemetry-client is being imported in the widget entry chunk and forcing parse on load.
Morgan: exact line is `import Telemetry from "@redwood/telemetry/client"` inside src/widgets/metrics/index.tsx — that file is bundled into the main widget chunk.
Sam: oh — we accidentally referenced Telemetry.init() at module top-level in the widget. that forces the module to load and run on first paint.
Tori: Which deploys included this change? deploy-bot: Deploy 2026.03.19-1217 pushed to canary by @ci/cd (commit d4c3b2f)
deploy-bot: Rollout: canary (10%) -> started 2026-03-19T12:17:03Z
telemetry-ingest-bot: Telemetry config update: client-default-sample-rate set to 0.2 for canary
Sam: quick repro locally after enabling telemetry flag — confirmed. Main-thread parse spikes from serialized schema + metric-mapper inside telemetry module.
Morgan: here's the offending snippet (from telemetry client):
```
// telemetry/client/index.ts
import { compileSchema } from './schema-compiler'
const compiled = compileSchema(defaultSchema)
export function init(opts){ /* attaches handlers, uses compiled */ }
```
Kevin: compileSchema is expensive and runs at import-time. we should lazy-compile on first init or do a dynamic import so the bundle stays small.
Alejandra: bundlewise this increased widget chunk by ~48KB gzipped. that seems small but parse-cost is killing UX on low-end devices.
Tori: Proposal: revert canary flag for telemetry augment now, open a targeted fix to lazy-import compileSchema and re-deploy to canary after validation.
Sam: I'll open a PR to change the widget to `const Telemetry = await import("@redwood/telemetry/client")` inside the setup function and memoize.
Kevin: also check that other widgets didn't import telemetry indirectly via shared-utils. run `npx source-map-explorer` on the bundle.
Alejandra: adding bundle analysis results to the issue: https://phab/internal/TELE-391
Morgan: also noticed KV cache miss correlation in traces — maybe telemetry warmup triggered heavy KV lookups. need to verify if telemetry touches kvcache on init.
telemetry-ingest-bot: Telemetry ingestion spike recorded at 2026-03-19T12:18:10Z — +4x baseline for canary hosts
Sam: repro + local patch ready, running perf sweep on slow phone emulator.
Tori: If the hotfix looks safe, let's do a fast rollback of the canary and push the lazy-load change behind a feature flag. I don't want a full rollback yet unless we see user impact.
Morgan: Agreed. Who can cut the canary rollback now?
Alejandra: I'll flip the canary flag and start a small rollback, then we can validate metrics in 10m.
Kevin: after rollback, we should add a bundling lint rule: no top-level telemetry import in widget entrypoints.
Sam: PR: #4208 drafted, includes dynamic import + fallback. running CI perf tests.
Alejandra: rollback done — canary lowered to 0%. watching charts.
telemetry-ingest-bot: Ingest rate normalized after canary rollback at 2026-03-19T12:28:01Z
Morgan: dashboards responsiveness looks back to normal in EU canary hosts. great job.
Tori: follow-ups: add unit for compileSchema to be lazy, update docs for telemetry client (explicit init), add bundle check in CI. I'll file tasks.
Kevin: also audit shared-utils for accidental re-exports so we don't reintroduce this.
Sam: will land the PR after perf CI green, then we can re-enable canary at 5% behind the new lazy-init.
Morgan: thanks everyone. filing a short postmortem and linking TELE-391 with timeline.
